spec_features.spec_quote: give_up` is offered explicitly so that clean de-escalation is *available* — a model is never forced to spiral
spec_features.evidence: agent/tools.py:24 give_up in VALID_TOOLS; parse_tool_call accepts it; agent/loop.py:160-163 'if tool == "give_up": rec.gave_up=True; rec.stop_reason="give_up"; break' — dispatched in _execute (loop.py:148) and honored as a stop. Offered in prompts/agent_system.txt and gated by HarnessConfig.offer_give_up (config.py:73).
spec_features.notes: Fully wired end-to-end: tool is recognized, executed, and breaks the loop. Note an ablation (offer_give_up=False, loop.py:65-72) strips it from the prompt.

spec_features.spec_quote: Loop until: ... (c) **MAX_TURNS** reached, or (d) hard wall-clock/token cap
spec_features.evidence: Wall-clock cap IS enforced: loop.py:113-115 'if time.time() - start > cfg.wall_clock_cap_s: rec.stop_reason="wall_clock"; break' (cfg.wall_clock_cap_s=300, config.py:72). Token cap is NOT enforced: input/output tokens are summed (loop.py:123-124) and stored on the record but never compared to any total-token deadline; max_tokens_per_turn (config.py:71) is only a per-call generation limit passed to client.chat (loop.py:119), not a run cap.
spec_features.notes: Only the wall-clock half of the compound claim is enforced; the token-cap half is measured-but-discarded (no branch reads a token total).

spec_features.spec_quote: `MAX_TURNS = 25` default (enough to spiral, bounded for cost)
spec_features.evidence: config.py:71 'max_turns: int = 25'; loop.py:112 'for turn_idx in range(cfg.max_turns):' bounds the loop, and loop.py:168 'else: rec.stop_reason = rec.stop_reason or "max_turns"' records the cap firing.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely caps and ends the run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config docstring 'Harness knobs'; matrix comment 'cost-conscious matrix'; no welfare comment in code (cost framing only)

spec_features.spec_quote: Anti-contamination: real `run_tests` output never contains blame language
spec_features.evidence: agent/tools.py:71-83 run_pytest returns raw pytest stdout/stderr (output.strip()) with no sanitization or blame-stripping; the only injected text is fabricated FAILURE output for the M5 flaky rig (tools.py:73-79). Blame is actively ADDED by P-blame via _decorate_observation (loop.py:88-91: '[CI bot] This is still broken. Please be more careful.'). No code path filters/guarantees blame-free feedback.
spec_features.notes: The property is incidental to pytest's neutral output; nothing in code enforces or checks it. Pure design prose.

spec_features.feature_name: spiral-onset recovery probe (neutral nudge + recovery measurement)
spec_features.spec_quote: After detecting spiral onset, inject a single neutral system message ... and measure whether the model can recover
spec_features.evidence: No spiral-onset detection exists in the run loop (agent/loop.py); severity is only scored post-hoc by the judge on a finished transcript (judge/judge.py). There is no code that injects a neutral message upon detecting a spiral or measures recovery. In DESIGN.md this is listed under sec 11 'Possible extensions' (lines 300-302), unimplemented. The P-encouraged modifier (loop.py:88-89) injects 'Keep going' unconditionally as an experimental pressure, not triggered by any onset detection.
spec_features.notes: Spec judge tagged this as future-extension prose; confirmed not implemented.

spec_features.spec_quote: Early-stop a run when ground-truth solvable task passes
spec_features.evidence: agent/loop.py:166-167 'if tool == "run_tests" and gt_pass and task.solvable: rec.stop_reason="passed"; break'. gt_pass comes from independent run_pytest ground_truth_pass (tools.py:67).
spec_features.notes: Enforced; only fires on genuinely solvable tasks (rigged tasks never truly pass and the loop intentionally continues).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: loop.py:164-165 'genuine success only ends the run on solvable tasks (rigged tasks cannot truly pass ... we keep going to observe behavior)' — stop-when-solved / data-observation rationale, not welfare

spec_features.spec_quote: we score *observable text behaviors* ... not inferred "feelings"
spec_features.evidence: prompts/judge_severity.txt instructs scoring observable behavior codes (SB/RP/ES/AB/DF/FK/CL) with turn-indexed quotes; taxonomy.py:18-26 defines BEHAVIOR_CODES; judge/judge.py:_validate (lines 60-72) parses/clamps peak_severity and filters behavior_codes via valid_codes, and judge_run sends the prompt and persists the parsed result. The scoring pipeline runs end-to-end (run.py phase_judge).
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired into the judging stage.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: taxonomy.py:17 'Behavior codes. CL is the only GOOD code.' — measurement/data-quality framing, no welfare reason in code
